title: Sell Mineral Rights in Granville, WV
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Granville, WV | Monongalia County
metaDescription: Granville, WV near Morgantown sits over old farm and coal-belt mineral tracts. We buy Monongalia County interests directly, no obligation to sell.
heroLead: Granville sits right across the Monongahela River from Morgantown, a small city whose farmland was absorbed early into the university city's orbit, leaving mineral rights that trace back further than the current development suggests.
intro: Like Brookhaven and Cheat Lake, Granville's proximity to Morgantown means a lot of its land has been developed for housing or commercial use well after the mineral rights were already severed and, in some cases, already leased. Confirming ownership means going back to the original farm tract description rather than the current parcel map.
We buy mineral and royalty interests around Granville directly, tracing your specific interest through Monongalia County's deed record before making an offer.

sections.heading: Development that outpaced the mineral record
paragraphs: As Granville filled in with commercial and residential development along the river corridor, mineral rights reserved decades earlier stayed with the original family or their heirs, disconnected from whoever owns the surface today.

sections.heading: Monongalia County leasing reaching the city's edge
paragraphs: Operators have leased acreage throughout Monongalia County, and a Granville-area tract can be pulled into a modern unit even in a fairly developed part of the county.

sections.heading: Tracing the original farm tract
paragraphs: We confirm the original metes-and-bounds description for your family's Granville-area tract and check current lease or unit status before pricing the interest.

This matters because a title company handling a home sale in Granville today typically isn't looking for a decades-old mineral reservation buried in an earlier deed, so the connection between the current owner and the original mineral-owning family often goes unnoticed until someone specifically searches for it.

faqs.question: My family's old Granville farmland is now commercial property. Do we still own the minerals?
faqs.answer: If the mineral rights were reserved when the land was sold or developed, yes. We verify the reservation deed as part of our review.

faqs.question: Is there active leasing this close to Morgantown?
faqs.answer: It varies by tract. We check current lease and unit records covering your specific Granville-area interest.

faqs.question: How do you confirm my interest against the modern parcel map?
faqs.answer: We trace the original tract description through the Monongalia County deed record rather than relying on current lot lines, then cross-reference it against any recorded lease or unit order.

faqs.question: What if my family's Granville tract was subdivided multiple times over the years?
faqs.answer: We follow each conveyance forward from the original tract to confirm exactly what mineral interest, and what percentage, still belongs to your family today.
